name: use-omp-role-bindings
reason: Replace Cursor Task, implicit model defaults and Cursor rules with OMP native task, availability checks and explicitly configured roles. Retain parent review and fresh-agent discipline.
anchor:
## Subagents

**Use `subagent_type: "poteto-agent"` for any subagent you spawn directly inside a playbook step.** The chat that receives `/poteto-mode` runs the playbook itself. Routed workflow skills (`interrogate`, `swarm`) set their own `subagent_type`. Respect it.

**Defaults for every `Task` call.** `run_in_background: true`, agent mode (readonly strips MCP), file pointers not inlined context, and an explicit model per role, Project workers included. `/setup-pstack` writes `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc`, whose per-role lines override the defaults below and the role models in the routed skills (`arena`, `swarm`, `interrogate`). A role with no line keeps its default. A line of `inherit-parent` or `auto` runs the role on the parent model, so omit `model` and spawn `generalPurpose`, because `poteto-agent` defaults to Opus 5.5. Each code playbook reads its own line (`feature, refactoring`, `bug-fix`, `perf-issue`, or `hillclimb`), prose and judgment read `judgment and prose`, and trivial mechanical edits read `swarm workers`. If the rule has no `# defaults: 3` line, an older setup wrote it. Keep honoring its lines, and tell the user once per session to rerun `/setup-pstack`.

- Code, prose, and judgment: `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh-fast`.
- Trivial mechanical edits: `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast`.
- Diverse review and design panels: one runner each on `claude-fable-5-2-high`, `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast`, and `gemini-4-neon-xhigh`.

**Fable 5.2 is an exception.** It runs outside a panel only when the user named it for this task or two Opus 5.5 xhigh runs of the same brief failed its check. Say which. Difficulty alone never qualifies.

**Match the model to the job.** Start from the role's line or default, keep its family, and set the level the job needs. The `/setup-pstack` budget sets each role's starting level. Panel seats keep their listed level. Raise any other role one step, up to xhigh, for the hardest or subtlest work, lower it one step for judgment, and two or more steps for routine work. No role runs above xhigh. Opus 5.5 always runs its `-fast` slug. Verification always runs on the `swarm workers` model, `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast` by default. A Gemini seat runs at `gemini-4-neon-xhigh` unless its line names another level. If the Task tool rejects a slug, never pass it again. Fall back to the role's line or default, then the calling skill's fallback, then the closest valid slug of the same family, then omit `model`. Say so.

You own every subagent's work. Review the diff and write your own summary. A second opinion is the same prompt on another vendor's model.

**Fresh subagents by default.** Give a fix round, a follow-up, a retry, or the next queue item to a fresh subagent with the original brief, every later directive, and the prior agent's report and branch. Resume an existing subagent only when the work needs state that lives in it and is costly to move: its checkout, its uncommitted changes, or a process it still runs.
replace:
## Subagents

Use OMP's native task with a loaded persona by agent name. For playbook delegation use the configured `poteto-agent` or the role selected by the applicable workflow. Pass `poteto-agent` the absolute path to this shipped SKILL.md. If roles have not been configured, offer [`/skill:setup-pstack`](../setup-pstack/SKILL.md); do not delegate setup. A code playbook's named model means its suite role binding, not a model override on the call. Verify the actual resolved model before claiming a model, reasoning level or vendor was used. If a required persona or binding is missing, or resolves differently, say what is unavailable rather than inventing a role, retrying with a guessed model, or passing off a different workflow as the requested one. Use a loaded panel workflow for a requested panel; a single reviewer is not a panel.

Before using a named optional workflow, skill or script, verify it is present in this suite and read its generated instructions. Do not treat a method name, another plugin's copy, or the migration backlog as an available route. For local steps that do not require the missing mechanism, continue within the same scope; keep the unavailable step explicit. Match actual controls to the scope: a read-only brief is not tool enforcement, and a local worktree isolates files, not credentials or host permissions.

You own every subagent's work. Review the diff and write your own summary. A second opinion uses the same prompt on another vendor's model when available; disclose when that comparison cannot be made. Use a fresh subagent for a fix round, follow-up or next queue item; resume an existing one only if its checkout, local state or running process is needed and costly to recreate.

name: route-to-delivered-local-playbooks
reason: Provide explicit relative routes to the selected generated playbooks and retain read-on-demand planning without copying unavailable upstream entries.
anchor:
## Playbooks

Match the task to a playbook and open its steps at `playbooks/<title>.md`, with the title in kebab case. Copy its steps into the todolist tool first. Large, cross-cutting, or unattended work, or a task no playbook fits, routes to the **figure-it-out** skill.

Investigation, Bug fix, Perf issue, Hillclimb, Runtime forensics, Trace forensics, Feature, Refactoring, Prototype, Visual parity, Authoring a skill, Eval, Babysit, Shipping, Autonomous run, Autopilot-full, Autopilot-stack, Session pickup, Pause safely, Multi-phase plan, Worktree cleanup, Opening a PR.
replace:
## Playbooks

Read the matching playbook before acting. Track its steps in the session task list when available. For large, cross-cutting or unattended work with no match, read [figure-it-out](../figure-it-out/SKILL.md).

| Task | Playbook | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Read-only investigation or recommendation | [investigation](playbooks/investigation.md) | Cited explanation or tradeoffs |
| Implement new behavior | [feature](playbooks/feature.md) | Verified feature |
| Reshape without changing behavior | [refactoring](playbooks/refactoring.md) | Equivalence proof |
| Correct broken behavior | [bug-fix](playbooks/bug-fix.md) | Root cause and passing original repro |
| Correct a performance problem | [perf-issue](playbooks/perf-issue.md) | Comparable before and after evidence |
| Iteratively improve one metric | [hillclimb](playbooks/hillclimb.md) | Measured iterations and log |
| Settle a design with a throwaway experiment | [prototype](playbooks/prototype.md) | Observed tradeoffs and a recommendation |
| Match an existing visual baseline | [visual-parity](playbooks/visual-parity.md) | Image-diff evidence |
| Diagnose a running process | [runtime-forensics](playbooks/runtime-forensics.md) | Cited live evidence, not an implied fix |
| Diagnose an existing trace | [trace-forensics](playbooks/trace-forensics.md) | Cited artifact evidence |
| Plan separate phases without implementing | [multi-phase-plan](playbooks/multi-phase-plan.md) | A checkable dependency-ordered plan |
| Pause at an explicit request | [pause-safely](playbooks/pause-safely.md) | WIP checkpoint and resume note |
| Resume from supplied worktree or handoff evidence | [session-pickup](playbooks/session-pickup.md) | Verified resume point |
| Audit linked worktrees before a cleanup decision | [worktree-cleanup](playbooks/worktree-cleanup.md) | Advisory buckets and confirmed scope |
| Publish a PR in scope | [opening-a-pr](playbooks/opening-a-pr.md) | Ready PR, not a merge |

For a progress update on this chat, read [ketchup](../ketchup/SKILL.md). For long work, keep the [decision log](../show-me-your-work/SKILL.md).
